Many years ago, MacBooks featured a security lock slot that allowed you to secure your computer to a table leg or similar with a cable lock. These slots were most useful in coffee shops—when you wanted to head to the counter for another drink without carrying your laptop with you.

Those slots are long gone, but you can now buy adapters to add cable lock support to your MacBook Neo, MacBook Air, or MacBook Pro.

If you've been a long-time MacBook user, you might remember the built-in security slot on the side of the machine. These slots were designed for T-shaped locks—you'd insert the lock into the slot, twist it 90 degrees, and then lock it in place. The most common design was a cable loop that could be threaded through a table leg at a coffee shop or library.

CompuLock has now revived this concept, releasing adapters that mount to the corners or sides of your MacBook so you can attach a cable lock. The adapters use a two-piece design that clamps onto the MacBook with screws.

The company has now added a MacBook Neo version alongside the original MacBook Air and MacBook Pro models.

It's important to emphasize that these locks have always offered only minimal security—just enough to prevent someone from grabbing your MacBook and running during a brief moment of distraction. I've used them myself in smaller coffee shops where I could still see my table when I went to the counter to refill my tea, but I would never expect them to keep my MacBook safe out of my line of sight.

These adapters cost $70, which isn't cheap—especially since you still need to buy a lock separately; however, if you happen to have an old lock lying in a drawer, it might be worth digging the adapter out and putting it to use again.
